purpose: Machine-readable API index for Ginject framework

core.responsibility: Application lifecycle, handler invocation, DI container

methods.name: Create
methods.purpose: Initialize app with module tree (MUST call once)

methods.name: EnableWS
methods.purpose: Enable WebSocket support; returns App for chaining

notes: No public setter exists to change the request body cap at runtime. maxRequestBodyBytes defaults to DefaultMaxRequestBodyBytes (10MB) in New() and is fixed for the life of the App. Do NOT invent a SetMaxBodySize-style method — it does not exist.

ServeHTTP unconditionally wraps r.Body in http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, app.maxRequestBodyBytes) before dispatching, independent of ctx.Init. Exceeding it surfaces as a 413 exception.RequestEntityTooLargeException from ctx.Body(), not a raw panic (see ctx.HTTPContext notes).
Listen() builds http.Server with DefaultReadHeaderTimeout=2s, DefaultReadTimeout=5s, DefaultWriteTimeout=15s, DefaultIdleTimeout=60s, DefaultMaxHeaderBytes=1MB — all hardcoded, no setters.

Module.description: Composition root for controllers and providers with lifecycle hooks
fields: IsGlobal bool - makes providers available to every module without an explicit import
OnInit func() - called during app.Create()'s module walk
OnReady func() - called once after app.Create() fully completes, in module-tree order
OnShutdown func() - called on graceful shutdown (SIGINT/SIGTERM, or app.Stop()), same module-tree order as OnReady (NOT reversed/LIFO)

ctx.responsibility: Request context objects and dependency types

methods: Status(code int) *HTTPContext - sets c.Code; chain with JSON/Text
Body() Body - lazily parses JSON body; on http.MaxBytesError panics exception.RequestEntityTooLargeException (413), not a raw error
HTTPContext.notes: No SetDeadline()/IsDeadlineExceeded()/Deadline field exist on HTTPContext — do not invent per-request deadline APIs. See metadata-concurrency-model.json's cancellation_handling for the real (server-level-only) timeout model.

common.responsibility: Pipeline interfaces and embedded controller types
notes: Guarder, Interceptable, and ExceptionFilterable are declared as `any`, NOT compile-time Go interfaces. Shape is checked at bind time via reflection (MethodByName) against the func-type aliases below. A bound value missing the method panics with a *ShapeError (GuardShapeError / InterceptorShapeError / ExceptionFilterShapeError).
MiddlewareFn IS a real interface (requires a Use method) — different from the other three.

interfaces.MiddlewareFn: interface { Use(*http.Request, http.ResponseWriter, ctx.Next) } — real interface; Use = func(*http.Request, http.ResponseWriter, ctx.Next) is the matching func alias
interfaces.Guarder: any; checked against HTTPCanActivate = func(*ctx.HTTPContext) bool via method name "CanActivate"
interfaces.Interceptable: any; checked against HTTPIntercept = func(*ctx.HTTPContext, *aggregation.Aggregation) any via method name "Intercept"
interfaces.ExceptionFilterable: any; checked against HTTPCatch = func(*ctx.HTTPContext, *exception.Exception) via method name "Catch" — NOTE: HTTPContext is the FIRST parameter, Exception is SECOND
interfaces.Logger: interface { Debug(msg string, args ...any); Info(...); Warn(...); Error(...); Fatal(...) } — no Log()/LogStructured() methods exist
interfaces.Publisher: interface { Publish(topic string, payload ...any) error } — payload is variadic, not a single `data any`

embedded_types.HTTP: Embed in controller to enable HTTP routing (there is NO common.REST type — do not generate it)
embedded_types.WS: Embed in controller to enable WebSocket routing
embedded_types.Middleware: Separate embeddable type providing BindMiddleware(MiddlewareFn, ...any) *Middleware — not a field on HTTP/WS

notes: Router.Match signature is func (r *Router) Match(method, route, version string) (bool, string, map[string][]int, []string, []ctx.HTTPHandler) — NOT (path, method) (RouterItem, bool). Do not invent a RouterItem-returning shape.

Exception.notes: No GetStackTrace()/SetStackTrace() and no stack-trace field exist. Exception{message, error, code} is the entire struct.

Event.notes: On/Once/Off/Emit all take variadic ...any, not a single `data any`/`fn func(any)` — a listener written as func(data any) does not satisfy func(args ...any) and will not compile.

trace.notes: No "handshake" stage exists. Interceptor is split into pre_interceptor/post_interceptor (two constants), not one combined "interceptor". Exception filter stage string is "exception_filter", not "filter".

memorybroker.responsibility: Lightweight in-process topic-based pub/sub broker (no queue groups, no persistence, no ack/retry)

Message.description: Published message (no ID, no Metadata — removed in simplification)
fields: Timestamp time.Time - captured via time.Now() before dispatch

pattern_types: Exact: 'user.login' - O(1) map lookup, matches only that topic
Suffix: 'user.*' - O(1) map lookup by prefix; greedy, matches ANY depth below 'user.', not just one level
Global: '*' - O(1), matches all topics. '*' is the ONLY wildcard token; '>' is NOT special-cased (verified empirically) - a pattern containing '>' matches only that literal string
Complex: 'user.*.profile', '*.created' - O(n) scan; segment-wildcard matching, NOT regex
key_features: Single sync.RWMutex over 4 maps (exact/prefix/global/complex) - no sharding
PublishAsync: one goroutine per call tracked by sync.WaitGroup, no worker pool/bounded queue
Close(): CompareAndSwap-idempotent, waits for in-flight PublishAsync via WaitGroup, then clears all maps
Cross-broker Unsubscribe protection via ErrForeignSubscription (checks subscription.broker == receiver)
Unsubscribe(nil) is always nil, unconditionally, even after Close
Unconditional panic recovery per handler call (not configurable, no OnPanic hook)
publishInternal sizes handler slice exactly, skips allocation entirely when nothing matches

memorycache.responsibility: In-memory sharded byte cache with TTL, no persistence

MemoryCache.description: In-memory cache, 256 shards, each an independently-locked map
constructors: NewMemoryCache(opts ...Option) *MemoryCache - the only constructor; no persistence variant exists
options: WithMaxEntries(n int) Option - caps total entries (default DefaultMaxEntries=100000); n<=0 means unlimited
methods: Set(ctx, key string, val []byte, ttl time.Duration) error
SetNX(ctx, key string, val []byte, ttl time.Duration) (bool, error)
Stop() - stops the background sweep goroutine; no flush, no persistence. NOT idempotent: calling it twice closes an already-closed channel and panics.

notes: No file-based persistence anywhere in this package. Do NOT invent PersistenceConfig / NewMemoryCacheWithConfig — they do not exist and never have in current source.
hashKey uses hash/maphash with a random per-process seed (not FNV-1a) — shard placement is stable within a process but not reproducible across restarts.

Eviction (admitLocked) is NOT LFU: on insert past the cap it samples up to 8 entries, deletes any already expired, and evicts whichever sampled entry has the soonest non-zero TTL (falls back to the first sampled entry if none have a deadline). It is an approximate cap, not an exact one.
key_characteristics: Approximate sampling-based eviction when WithMaxEntries cap is hit (see notes — not LFU)
Automatic background sweep every 5s/256 shards, stopped by Stop()
Thread-safe all operations except Stop() double-call (see notes)

critical_rules: NEVER hold onto context after request completes
NEVER mutate context after guard stage
NEVER panic in guard (return bool instead)
NEVER call next() multiple times in middleware
NEVER access raw websocket.Conn in handlers (use Publisher)
NEVER retain pooled objects beyond request lifetime
Module initialization order is SACRED - do not reorder
common_mistakes: Type mismatch between provider and handler parameter
Calling next() multiple times in middleware
Slow clients causing message drops in WebSocket
